title: Non-Hermitian Cooperation Induced Chern Insulator
authors: Weiwei Zhu, Bingbing Wang, Mengxiang Xie, Hong-yu Zou, Yang Long, Hong-xiang Sun, Haoran Xue, Jie Ren
abstract: Conventional Chern insulators rely on breaking time-reversal symmetry via magnetic fields or synthetic gauge fields. Here we introduce a fundamentally different paradigm: a static lattice without any gauge field becomes a Chern insulator solely through the cooperation of two non-Hermitian ingredients: on-site loss and non-reciprocal coupling. Neither effect alone suffices; only their synergy opens a topological gap and gives rise to robust chiral edge states with a nonzero Chern number. The underlying mechanism originates from a non-Hermitian chiral molecule formed by the lossy sites, whose dynamically dominant mode carries an orbital angular momentum that effectively generates a synthetic flux after the fast-decaying degrees of freedom are eliminated. Our results establish non-Hermitian cooperation as a versatile resource for inducing Chern topology without external fields or temporal modulations, opening a new route to topological phases in open classical and quantum systems.
summary: This paper demonstrates that a Chern insulator can be realized in a static lattice solely by combining on-site loss and non-reciprocal couplings, bypassing the need for external magnetic fields. The mechanism involves the slow-decaying mode of a chiral non-Hermitian molecule generating an effective synthetic magnetic flux. This establishes non-Hermitian cooperation as a powerful new resource for topological engineering in open systems.
main_problem: To establish a fundamentally new paradigm for inducing Chern topology in a static lattice without relying on external magnetic fields, synthetic gauge potentials, or pre-existing Hermitian topology.
main_result: The synergy between on-site loss and non-reciprocal coupling is sufficient to open a topological gap and generate robust chiral edge states with a quantized Chern number.
method: The mechanism is analyzed by projecting the full Hamiltonian onto the dynamically dominant mode of a non-Hermitian chiral molecule, effectively mapping the system to a synthetic Hofstadter model.
model_or_system: The model uses a static lattice structure containing four non-Hermitian sites, characterized by on-site loss ($-i\gamma$) and non-reciprocal couplings ($\kappa e^{\pm \alpha}$). The system is analyzed via its Bloch Hamiltonian, which is block-form.
key_observables: Quantized Chern number (C), chiral edge states, and the effective synthetic magnetic flux ($\pi/2$ per plaquette).
important_parameters:
The coexistence regime ($\gamma 
eq 0$ and $\alpha 
eq 0$) is crucial; individual non-Hermitian effects are insufficient.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a projection reduction technique that eliminates fast-decaying degrees of freedom to isolate the slowest-decaying, dynamically dominant mode.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the lattice structure, the spectral analysis of the chiral molecule, the resulting effective Hofstadter unit cell, and the projected band structures showing gap opening only in the coexistence regime.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem of field-free topology, then details the Hamiltonian structure involving loss and non-reciprocity. The core of the work involves analyzing the chiral molecule's dynamics and projecting the system to reveal the effective synthetic flux, culminating in the calculation of the non-zero Chern number.
why_interesting: This work provides a general theoretical framework for engineering topological phases using only intrinsic non-Hermitian couplings, which is highly relevant for designing open quantum systems and non-reciprocal devices.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Non-Hermitian cooperation enables a Chern insulator. (a) Schematic of the finite lattice structure. The unit cell is marked by a dashed box, and four lossy sites (blue) form a chiral non-Hermitian ”molecule”. (b) Enlarged view of a single unit cell, showing the real couplings t (solid black lines), on-site loss −iγ (blue dots), and non-reciprocal couplings κe±α (blue directed lines, with arrows indicating the hopping direction) (c) Strip geometry used for band calculations, with periodic boundary conditions along x and open boundaries along y. (d)–(g) Projected band structures under four conditions: (d) Hermitian limit (γ = 0, α = 0); (e) only asymmetric couplings (γ = 0, α = 1);...

Fig. 2. Non-Hermitian chiral molecule, spectral properties, and the effective Hofstadter model. (a) The four lossy sites are extracted from the full lattice to form a non-Hermitian chiral ”molecule” with non-reciprocal couplings κe±α and on-site loss −iγ. (b) Complex eigenvalue spectrum of the chiral molecule in the coexistence regime [κ = 1, γ = 2 sinh(1), α = 1]. The slowest-decaying mode (red dot, with the smallest imaginary part in magnitude) is well separated from three highly lossy modes (green dots), rendering it dynamically dom- inant. (c) Eigenstate of the dominant mode, showing a phase wind- ing of 2π around the four sites, indicating that it carries an orbital angular momentum....

Fig. 3. Finite-lattice spectra and field profiles validating the topolog- ical protection against local perturbations. (a) Eigenenergy spectrum of a finite 10 × 10 lattice with open boundary conditions; a represen- tative edge state is marked by a green dot. (b) Spatial distribution of the field amplitude for the green-marked edge state, illustrating its boundary localization. (c) Eigenenergy spectrum of the same lattice but with intentionally introduced defects; the persistent edge state (green dot) remains inside the bulk gap. (d) Field profile of the edge state in the defective lattice, demonstrating the robustness of topo- logical edge state.
